title: Follow evidence through a Prometheus deployment
description: Switch paths to separate discovery and scraping, local storage, rule evaluation, alert delivery, and asynchronous remote write. Inspect a node for its exact responsibility.

nodes.label: Service discovery
nodes.detail: Produces target labels and addresses. Relabeling decides which discovered targets become scrape targets and which labels are retained.

nodes.label: Target or exporter
nodes.detail: Exposes current metric families over HTTP. It owns instrumentation quality, label bounds, and scrape response time.

nodes.label: Scrape engine
nodes.detail: Selects targets, performs timed scrapes, applies metric relabeling, records scrape health, and appends accepted samples.

nodes.label: Local TSDB + WAL
nodes.detail: Stores the mutable head and persisted blocks used by local queries and rules. The WAL protects recent local writes across restart but is not clustered replication.

nodes.label: Rule engine
nodes.detail: Evaluates recording and alerting rules on intervals. Recording results return to the TSDB; active alerts are sent to configured Alertmanagers.

nodes.label: Remote-write queue
nodes.detail: Reads WAL samples into sharded queues, batches requests, retries failures, and adds memory, CPU, and network pressure.

nodes.label: Alertmanager
nodes.detail: Groups, deduplicates, routes, silences, and inhibits alerts. It does not evaluate the alert's PromQL expression.

nodes.label: Remote storage
nodes.detail: Accepts remote-write batches under its own durability, query, tenancy, and availability contract.

nodes.label: On-call receiver
nodes.detail: Receives a routed notification and needs enough context, ownership, and runbook evidence to act.

scenarios.label: Healthy scrape
scenarios.summary: Discovery supplies an eligible target, the HTTP scrape succeeds, and accepted samples enter the local TSDB.
scenarios.result: Prometheus records the target's samples and an up value of 1 for the successful scrape. Local queries and later rule evaluations can use the new samples.

scenarios.label: Target down
scenarios.summary: The target is discovered but the scrape request times out or returns an invalid response.
scenarios.result: Prometheus records up as 0 for the failed scrape and does not receive the target's application samples. Existing stored history remains queryable.

scenarios.label: Rule to page
scenarios.summary: A rule reads local series, remains active for its configured duration, and sends a firing alert for Alertmanager to route.
scenarios.result: Prometheus owns detection state; Alertmanager owns grouping and notification policy. Both paths need independent health checks.

scenarios.label: Slow rule group
scenarios.summary: A rule group has not finished before its next scheduled evaluation.
scenarios.result: Prometheus skips the next evaluation of that group until the current evaluation completes or times out, creating a gap in recorded or alert evidence.

scenarios.label: Alertmanager down
scenarios.summary: PromQL alert state is firing, but the configured Alertmanager cannot accept the alert update.
scenarios.result: Detection remains visible in Prometheus, but grouping and receiver delivery are unavailable. Prometheus periodically resends alert state, so recovery must be tested end to end.

scenarios.label: Remote write down
scenarios.summary: Local ingestion continues while the remote endpoint rejects or cannot receive batches.
scenarios.result: The remote-write queue retries and consumes resources. If the endpoint remains unavailable beyond the retained WAL window, unsent remote samples can be lost even though local data was ingested.

scenarios.label: Local disk loss
scenarios.summary: The Prometheus node loses its unsupported or failed local storage volume.
scenarios.result: Local query history and rule inputs are unavailable because the built-in TSDB is not clustered or replicated. Recovery depends on tested snapshots, another autonomous replica, or the separately designed remote-storage contract.
